summary: Kept authenticated local encryption but reduced macOS Keychain resolution to one attempt per process and data-directory account, including denial/error paths.
Made explicit 32-byte test keys take precedence over the deterministic in-process test override.
Corrected the cache claim to three managed tiers plus resident llama.cpp live sequence state.
Bounded encrypted persistent cache storage to 64 entries and 2 GiB with transactional LRU eviction and blob deletion.
Made missing, malformed, or unauthenticated persistent cache state invalidate and fall back instead of failing chat.
Proved both explicit persona-pack restore and automatic session-checkpoint reuse across fresh CLI processes with a real local GGUF.

tests_run.detail: Includes 31 runtime unit tests, 18 deterministic runtime integration tests, cache selector/fingerprint tests, CLI tests, and readiness tests.
67 commands, 76 affordances, 25 effects, 36 parity rows, 58 upstream settings, zero blockers.

storage_evidence.key_source: macOS Keychain installation key, or explicit test key
storage_evidence.keychain_lookup_bound: one attempt per process and data-directory account; success and denial/error are both cached until relaunch
tested: metadata and blob mutations commit or roll back together
concurrent mutations do not lose writes
installation-key provider called once on success
denied installation key not retried until relaunch

cache_evidence.resident_engine_state: live sequence state is an engine context, not advertised as a fourth managed cache tier
tested: bounded memory LRU and hit promotion
cross-tier longest-prefix and memory tie selection
transactional persistent eviction and old-blob deletion
missing and authenticated-corrupt blob invalidation with fallback
real automatic session checkpoint reuse in a fresh process

honest_boundary: A rebuilt ad-hoc-signed development app can still receive one macOS Keychain authorization prompt; repeated store opens in that process cannot produce repeated lookups.
Encryption protects copied app files, not an attacker controlling the running app or unlocked user account.
The real cache proof used the available SmolLM2 GGUF on CPU; Gemma 4 remains the product release-model acceptance gate.
